SLIDES:
It’s a kind of machine.

Start with the group it belongs to: a kind of machine / tool / container. This alone gets you halfway.

You use it to record things. — It’s used for recording things.

Two ways to say what it does. use it to + verb, but used for + -ing.

It’s a thing which you put into the wall.

which or that introduces what the object does. Both are correct here.

It’s long and thin, like a stick. It looks like a mobile phone.

Compare it with something the other person definitely knows.

I’ve forgotten the word. Do you know what I mean?

Hand the turn back. This is what keeps the conversation alive instead of stopping it.

Warm-up: They only have to recognise the object. Producing the descriptions is stage 6.
5 minutes. Item 5 is the hard one; leave it if the class is slow.
Vocabulary: The seven phrases are vocabulary items here, not grammar. Drill them as single units.
Noun from disappoint. Point at the suffix; it comes back in the Unit Test.
How it works: group, function, comparison, hand back. If a student can do those four, they can talk around any missing word.
used for record and use it for record. It is used for recording or use it to record.
Practice: This is the transfer task — describing objects they genuinely do not know the word for. Expect it to be slow.
Articles and quantifiers together. Do not skip it.
Conversations: Play each one twice. The customer never knows the word; the assistant always guesses it.
Do not go straight to writing. The three model tasks are the lesson.
Now you: The spoken round makes the written complaint much easier.
Collect the emails and comment on them after the speaking, not during.
Wrap: Articles from Lesson 13 and quantifiers from Lesson 14. Both are in the model email.

Stage 1 · Warm-up

What are they talking about?

Somebody has forgotten the English word. They describe it instead. Can you work out what it is?

Read each description and choose the object.

You do not have to describe anything yet. Just recognise it.

1“It’s a thing you keep money in. It’s small, it’s often made of leather, and it goes in your pocket.”
2“It’s long and thin, like a stick, and you burn it. You need one when there’s no electricity.”
3“It’s used for making water hot. It’s metal or plastic and it lives in the kitchen.”
4“It’s a kind of cable. You put one end in the wall and the other end in your phone.”
5“It’s made of metal, and you move cheese up and down against it. Do you know what I mean?”
Talk about it
  • Work in pairs. Which description was easiest? Which was hardest? Why?
  • When did you last forget a word in English and have to explain it?
Talk about it
  • Tell your teacher when you last forgot a word in English and had to explain your way around it.
Write it down

Write about one time you forgot a word in English. What did you say instead?

Now speak — ask and answer these questions with a partner.
Answer these two out loud before you go on.

1  What do you do when you do not know a word in English?

2  When did you last complain about something you had bought?

Then tell the class the one most surprising thing about your partner.

Stage 3 · Grammar

Talking around a missing word

You will never know every word. What you can learn is how to get to the word without having it.

Read these four lines from the recordings in stage 5.
  • It’s a kind of machine.
  • You use it to record things. — It’s used for recording meetings.
  • It’s a thing which you put into the wall.
  • It looks like a mobile phone. It’s long and thin, like a stick.
Which two say exactly the same thing in different words?
Four moves, in this order
MovePatternExample
1 · the groupIt’s a kind of + nounIt’s a kind of container.
2 · what it doesYou use it to + verb
It’s used for + verb-ing		You use it to open bottles.
It’s used for opening bottles.
2 · what it doesIt’s a thing which / that + clauseIt’s a thing which you put in the wall.
3 · comparisonIt looks like + noun · It’s like + noun
It’s made of + material		It looks like a pen. It’s made of metal.
4 · hand it backWhat’s it called? · Do you know what I mean?
I’ve forgotten the word in English.		… you know, for the kitchen. Do you know what I mean?
Articles recycledIt’s a kind of machine · It’s made of — metal · The one I mean is bigger.
Quantifiers recycledThere isn’t much room inside · It’s got a few buttons on the side
The rules that matter
  • Start with the group, not the detail. It’s a kind of tool tells the listener more than three sentences about its shape.
  • Two patterns, two forms: use it to + plain verb, but used for + -ing. Mixing them is the commonest error at this level.
  • which and that are both fine after a thing. Do not say a thing what.
  • Always hand the turn back. A description that ends with Do you know what I mean? gets an answer; one that just stops does not.
  • Everything you built in Lessons 13 and 14 — articles and quantifiers — is inside these descriptions.
Full grammar reference — Explaining a word, and complaining

Form

Putting it in a groupIt’s a kind of bag. · It’s a sort of tool.
Saying what it doesIt’s used for cutting. · You use it to open bottles.
Defining itIt’s a thing which keeps food cold. · It’s the person who serves you.
CheckingWhat’s it called in English? · Do you know what I mean?
Complaining in writingI am writing to complain about… · I would like a refund. · I look forward to your reply.

When and why we use it

  • When you do not know a word, do not stop — describe the group, then the use, then the place.
  • Used for is followed by -ing; used to + verb means something different (Unit 11).
  • A formal complaint keeps to facts: what you ordered, what arrived, what you want.
  • Formal writing avoids short forms: I am, not I’m.

Signal words

a kind of · a sort of · something like · you know, the one that…

Watch out — the mistakes learners really make

  • It’s used for cut bread. → It’s used for cutting bread.Used for + -ing.
  • It’s a thing who opens bottles. → It’s a thing which opens bottles.Which for things.
  • I write to complain. → I am writing to complain.The fixed opening is in the continuous.
  • I want my money back now. → I would like a refund.Formal register.

Don’t confuse it with

It’s used for opening (its purpose) against I used to open (a past habit, Unit 11).

5 · Read the model email. This is what you will write in the next stage.

Subject: Order 48–2291 — wrong item received

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about an order I received on 14 March (order number 48–2291).

I ordered a black leather laptop bag. The bag that arrived is the right colour, but it is made of plastic, and it is far too small for a laptop. It is also in poor condition — there is a mark on the front.

I have already sent two messages through your website and I have not had any reply yet.

I would like a full refund, and I am happy to return the bag at your expense.

I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Dana Sultanova

Note. Written for this course as a writing model. The order number, the company and the customer are invented.
